key_headlines.title: Naphtha designated as economic security item; Public utility fees frozen if possible
key_headlines.summary: President Lee Jae-myung announced naphtha's designation as an economic security item and the freezing of public utility fees in the first half to counter supply chain instability from the Middle East. Emergency logistics cost vouchers will also be introduced to stabilize the economy.

key_headlines.title: February import prices rose 1.1%, 8th consecutive month of increase; driven by Middle East tensions and rising oil prices
key_headlines.summary: South Korea's import prices increased by 1.1% in February, marking the eighth consecutive monthly rise, primarily due to escalating international oil prices stemming from the US-Iran conflict. This indicates growing inflationary pressures from external factors.

key_headlines.title: Middle East buyers unreachable, shipments halted; SMEs face export disruptions and capital crunch
key_headlines.summary: Small and medium-sized enterprises (SMEs) are experiencing severe export disruptions and cash flow problems as Middle Eastern buyers become unreachable and shipments are delayed due to the prolonged war. This situation is leading to a significant increase in inventory and a worsening of working capital shortages.

key_headlines.title: Refineries' crude oil inventory could be depleted this month; Domestic jet fuel production drop threatens global supply
key_headlines.summary: Korean refineries' crude oil inventories are projected to be depleted by the end of this month due to the prolonged US-Iran war, raising concerns about disruptions to South Korea's role as the world's largest jet fuel exporter. This could lead to potential shocks in the global aviation market.

key_headlines.title: If Iran situation continues for 1 year, South Korea's growth rate could fall to '0% range'
key_headlines.summary: A report by NH Financial Research Institute warns that South Korea's annual economic growth rate could plummet to the 0% range if the Iran conflict persists for over a year. Scenarios in the report outline potential economic impacts and necessary response measures.

sections.Hot Economy News: The Korean economy is under significant pressure from the ongoing Middle East conflict, leading to the government designating naphtha as an economic security item and freezing public utility fees to mitigate supply chain risks. Import prices are rising, impacting inflation, while small and medium-sized enterprises face severe export disruptions and a capital crunch. Furthermore, domestic crude oil inventories are at risk of depletion, which could severely affect global jet fuel supply. Analysts warn that a prolonged conflict could significantly curb South Korea's economic growth, potentially pushing it to the 0% range.
sections.Macro & Fiscal Policy: Bank of Korea Monetary Policy Board members hold diverse opinions on the benchmark interest rate, though some note the current exchange rate is not a major worry. While the Middle East conflict exerts significant pressure on inflation and growth, BOK member Lee Soo-hyung believes it is not an immediate monetary policy concern, but acknowledges increased uncertainty. High oil prices have notably contributed to a 1.1% rise in February's import prices, particularly raw materials, and are expected to burden even low-inflation economies like China.
sections.Financial Markets: The KOSPI index closed at 5,640, paring earlier gains, while the KOSDAQ index experienced a decline. Bank of Korea Monetary Policy Board members, after maintaining the benchmark interest rate for six consecutive times, emphasized the stability of the exchange rate and real estate market as key considerations. They also noted stronger economic growth than anticipated as a factor against further rate cuts. The won-dollar exchange rate showed minor fluctuations, reflecting ongoing market volatility.
sections.Industry & Technology: Posco International saw its target price increased due to strong energy and battery material business prospects. Korean battery manufacturers are facing intense competition in government ESS tenders amid a slump in EV demand, prompting concerns about excessive price wars. Despite the 'EV chasm,' LG Energy Solution secured a significant battery contract with Tesla in the US, and Samsung SDI also expanded its ESS battery business in North America. Meanwhile, SK Incheon Petrochemical sold its stake in Oilhub Korea Yeosu to secure liquidity and refocus on core growth areas like batteries.
sections.Real Estate: Despite past failures, 'half-price apartments' (land-lease units) in Magok saw immense popularity with a 67.9:1 subscription rate, demonstrating strong demand for affordable housing amidst escalating prices. However, Seoul's housing purchase sentiment sharply declined in February, contrasting with stable rental sentiment, indicating a divided market. A prolonged national shortage of new housing supply is also driving high interest in any newly available developments across the country.
sections.International Economy: The US Federal Reserve faces internal divisions and a complex decision regarding interest rates at its upcoming FOMC meeting amidst the US-Iran conflict. While a rate freeze is widely anticipated, rising oil prices due to potential disruptions in the Strait of Hormuz are fueling inflation concerns, which could push the Fed toward a hawkish stance. Former President Trump's requests for allied military support in the region have been met with reluctance, highlighting international tensions. The volatility in energy prices is adding significant uncertainty to the global economic outlook.
sections.AI & Economy: The AI sector is showing strong economic impact, with Powernet's stock surging due to high demand for AI infrastructure and server power solutions, and Shinsegae I&C also hitting its upper limit on news of its potential entry into AI data center business. The Korea Institute for Advancement of Technology is actively discussing strategies to develop a robust humanoid industry ecosystem, emphasizing the need for integrated hardware and software. Furthermore, local startups are achieving notable success in AI-driven products like smart glasses, indicating broader economic integration of AI.
sections.Others: Venezuela continues to face severe economic hardship, characterized by hyperinflation and reduced oil output, despite political changes, leading to widespread public discontent. Internationally, allied nations are cautiously avoiding direct military involvement in the US-Iran conflict, despite requests for support from former President Trump to ensure the opening of the Strait of Hormuz. Meanwhile, investors are betting on declining oil prices, expecting the strait to remain open. Domestically, Korean game companies are re-electing leadership to focus on AI as a key growth engine. China is emerging as a dominant player in the AI glasses market, forecast to produce almost half of the global supply this year.
